newsitem.title: GERMANY: German wheat eases on EU export tax, weather.
newsitem.headline: German wheat eases on EU export tax, weather.

text.p: German wheat prices are drifting lower following Brussels' decision to tax European Union wheat exports and because European crop weather is favourable, brokers said on Tuesday.
Pressure also came from a pile-up of marketable old crop wheat, with consumers mostly covered until harvest time, and from French wheat offers in Germany's southwest.
Brokers said long-awaited rainfall in France, Britain, southern Europe and Germany was now pointing to a good 1997 wheat crop and the area had been expanded by four percent.
But area reductions in Canada and the U.S., combined with low global stocks and good demand, should underpin 1997/98 world market prices.
The Hamburg grain exchange kept its wheat (12.5 percent, 220 Hagberg) price free Hamburg at 285 marks a tonne and left the spot feed wheat price unchanged at 280.
But fob Baltic sellers cut nominal May delivery wheat by between 1.50 and 5.00 marks on the week.
They quoted 12 percent protein wheat at 280-296.50 marks and material with 13/14 percent protein at 287.50-316.50 marks.
Fob Baltic barley offers were unchanged at 273.50 marks.
Rye was down by up to five marks down at 267.50-270 marks as bread rye demand was weakening and feed rye prices drifted closer towards intervention price levels.
New crop grain was mostly untraded and sellers cut nominal wheat prices by 2.50-5.00 marks.
Fob Baltic September wheat with 12 percent protein was at parity with May at 280 marks.
New crop rye indications are at around 265 marks and barley was set at 242.50-257.50, depending on port and shipment date.
